nodes.notes:
- Classification: mixed dense matrix contractions, causal triangular masking, prefix-scan-derived elementwise decay, and sequence reductions. Output is dense Y[b,c,i,h,d]; state and source-position dimensions are reduced. chunk_size, heads, head_dim, groups, and state_size are fixed; batch and chunk counts vary.
- Canonical math: for g=floor(h/4), Y[b,c,i,h,d]=sum_{j=0..i}(sum_s C[b,c,i,g,s]*B[b,c,j,g,s])*exp(sum_{k=j+1..i} A[b,h,c,k])*X[b,c,j,h,d]. Batch, chunk, group, and target-position tiles are independent. FP32 accumulation should be retained; G and decay-weighted source contributions may be streamed.
- Layout: X[b,c,j,h,d] is BF16 with contiguous d; A[b,h,c,k] is BF16 with contiguous k; B/C[b,c,j,g,s] are BF16 with contiguous s; Y has contiguous d. B/C reuse spans four heads, C reuse spans source positions, B reuse spans target positions, and each decay sequence is reused over d. Fixed 128-element vectors and tiles can be staged in registers or shared memory.
- Regimes: small B*C (1-4) is launch- and occupancy-sensitive; medium B*C has enough parallelism and is likely tensor-core compute-bound; large B*C (up to 512) is throughput-bound with pressure from G/X traffic; numerically extreme A values can make FP32 exp and accumulation behavior the limiter regardless of size.
- Knobs: explicit versus recomputed G, per-head versus four-head group ownership, target/source/state/head-dimension tiling, persistent versus conventional scheduling, register/shared staging, causal tile pruning, BF16 versus FP32 storage of G or M, FP32 exp, and specialized paths for small versus large B*C.
- Skeleton: form a B/C contraction tile in FP32; derive inclusive A prefixes once per head and obtain decay as exp(prefix[i]-prefix[j]) under j<=i; combine G and decay; reduce against X into FP32 output accumulators; cast once to BF16. Synchronization is only needed when a program shares staged B/C or G data across warps.
- Pruned families: explicit shared-G factorization maximizes four-head reuse but adds an intermediate; independent-head contraction minimizes coordination but recomputes G; four-head group contraction avoids G traffic but risks register pressure and duplicated work across d tiles.

kernel_summary: This is a fixed-shape, dense mixed contraction and causal-scan kernel: each output combines a group-shared B/C state contraction over 128 states with a head-specific lower-triangular exponential decay and a reduction over 128 source positions. The eager reference is dominated by enormous expanded L, M, and broadcast-product intermediates, while an effective Triton implementation should be primarily tensor-core compute-bound after eliminating those tensors. The central tradeoff is whether to materialize the 128x128 G matrix once per group or fuse it with output production; H100 favors the fixed 128 contraction dimensions, but four-head reuse, FP32 exponential/accumulation, small-workload launch latency, and register pressure determine the best family.
